tasks.title: Establish neutral benchmark package and calibrated substrate
expectedOutputs: A standalone @exharness/benchmark workspace package owns substrate-independent experiment registration, attempt/evidence/accounting and audit contracts without importing ExHarness product runtime packages.

A pinned Harbor adapter and deterministic calibration workload prove fresh reset, independent verification, artifact extraction, evidence reopening and orthogonal failure/accounting semantics before any harness-value claim.

The retired scripts/delivery/baseline Direct/Core value-study implementation is removed from current benchmark execution paths after replacement calibration passes; Git history retains historical evidence.
BB-065 establishes benchmark trustworthiness only. Direct-versus-ExHarness harness economics, component attribution and product-value conclusions remain downstream.

tasks.title: Integrate a real coding-agent execution strategy
expectedOutputs: A real agent edits the declared fixture through runtimeAdapter.dispatch and reports exact execution and source evidence.
Fresh-process recover reuses the same attempt/session or reports an explicit unresolved outcome; it cannot silently create a second semantic attempt.
Pinned strategy/config and authorized scope survive policy change, timeout and cancellation; runtime success never self-accepts delivery.

tasks.title: Enforce bounded workspace and tool capabilities
expectedOutputs: Forbidden file, cross-workspace and credential access fail under the selected sandbox threat model, including indirect tool calls.
Time/token/cost ceilings stop further dispatch and preserve a recoverable outcome; secrets are absent from persisted traces.
Untrusted repository/MCP content cannot grant tools, change authorized domains or bypass approval for configured protected operations.

tasks.title: Connect real repository changes to CI and review evidence
expectedOutputs: The candidate records base SHA, exact resulting commit/tree, changed files and CI run identities from the real provider.
A deliberate failing check returns bounded repair; stale checks and unrelated branch updates cannot satisfy candidate acceptance.
Retry after lost provider acknowledgement discovers the existing change or blocks on ambiguity; it does not create duplicate review requests or bypass merge policy.

tasks.title: Prove first useful agent delivery through Oracle and independent QA
expectedOutputs: The real feature uses Oracle-resolved exact input refs, produces a real candidate and runs in an isolated preview whose release identity is recorded.
Independent QA observes functional behavior and rejects a seeded defect even when the producer says success.
At least three reset live runs and one kill/resume path have complete evidence, budgets and failure records; feasibility is reported separately from pilot value.

tasks.title: Deliver product from goal and partial artifacts across owned domains
expectedOutputs: Goal-only, requirements/design and existing-code seeds converge to the same declared acceptance semantics with actual product evidence.
FE and BE can progress independently where obligations allow; domain publication creates authorized obligations without selecting another domain's runtime.
Missing authoritative product decisions pause for the owner; current deployment/QA/completeness evidence is required for product outcome closure.

tasks.title: Prove requirement change and failure recovery on a live product
expectedOutputs: A real requirement change invalidates only affected outputs and drives the owning domains to a newly verified release.
Kill/resume and duplicate activation preserve attempt identity and one logical external publication.
An old worker and stale deployment observation cannot close changed work; unrelated accepted outputs remain current.

tasks.title: Make delivery runs observable recoverable and cost bounded
expectedOutputs: A fresh operator can explain blockers and inspect exact task/attempt/model/runtime/SCM identities without model-inferred provenance.
Cost and duration include failed/retried provider calls; missing usage is explicit and cannot appear as zero.
Backup/restore and process restart recover canonical runs; lost telemetry cannot grant or revoke product acceptance.

tasks.title: Ship an installable supported delivery profile
expectedOutputs: A fresh environment installs a pinned release and completes the reference delivery with documented configuration.
Health checks and actionable errors cover missing credentials, unsupported runtime and incompatible persisted state.
Upgrade and rollback exercises preserve or explicitly gate ongoing attempt compatibility; runbooks document support boundaries.

tasks.title: Measure delivery-harness value under a controlled benchmark program
expectedOutputs: Run a preregistered harness comparison with fixed model snapshot, task input, workspace, prompt contract, resource ceilings, artifact extraction and evaluator; include an external/public workload plus ExHarness delivery-lifecycle workloads and held-out tasks.

Report all attempts as a multidimensional profile: accepted quality, cost/tokens per accepted delivery, lead time, human active effort, repeated-run consistency, fault robustness and harness failure fingerprints; do not collapse the result into one opaque score.

Exercise delivery-specific scenarios including verifier rejection and repair, stale context, process kill/resume, session handoff, provider ambiguity, CI failure and dependency/currentness fencing so lifecycle value is measured separately from coding pass rate.
A failed or inconclusive preregistered gate yields an explicit no-go or follow-up scope; no value claim may be inferred from selected successful demonstrations.

tasks.title: Validate one useful HOW improvement on held-out delivery tasks
expectedOutputs: Select one HOW candidate from an observed benchmark failure fingerprint or ablation result, not from an architecture preference, and freeze product semantics plus resource ceilings before evaluation.
Evaluate the candidate on held-out tasks with the same model/harness benchmark contract and report paired quality-cost-latency-human-effort deltas plus new failure modes.
Independent evaluation supports PROMOTE or KEEP_BASELINE only from the preregistered evidence; acceptance semantics and producer-authored success claims cannot be changed after results.
Existing attempts remain pinned, new attempts use a promoted strategy only after authorization, and regression can trigger supported rollback.

tasks.title: Accept supported product release with independently reproducible value
expectedOutputs: All prerequisite feature evidence is delivered and the exact release reproduces supported entry, change, recovery, handoff and independent QA behavior.
A clean operator environment reproduces installation, a representative delivery and the benchmark protocol on the exact release; documentation states the supported harness/model/runtime profile.
Release evidence includes the multidimensional benchmark profile and known limitations, with no claim based solely on source merge, CI, agent success or a single aggregate benchmark score.

tasks.title: Research harness-isolation economics on shared benchmark kernel
expectedOutputs: DIRECT_CODEACT and CORE_SYNC are experiment-specific arm adapters over the delivered @exharness/benchmark kernel and calibrated substrate, not owners of generic runner/accounting/evidence infrastructure.
A fixed-factor protocol, cohort/repeat schedule and harness-economics reducer isolate synchronous harness effects while preserving every attempt and UNKNOWN/null provider observations.
BB-077 emits only comparison-specific metrics/reporting and a held-out handoff for BB-081; generic AttemptLedger/evidence/accounting/audit remain BB-065 ownership.
Worker execution remains blocked on BB-065 delivery even when research readiness converges.

tasks.title: Integrate async steering, wakeup and recovery
expectedOutputs: User steering while operations run with one-model-in-flight invariant preserved.
Deterministic completion coalescing that avoids unnecessary model-turn storms.
Kill/restart and cancellation recovery with exact pending-operation identity.

tasks.title: Research held-out harness profile acceptance and fault-ablation protocol
expectedOutputs: Define a held-out ablation matrix over the synchronous baseline and BB-078/079/080 capabilities so detached operations, cache-stable context and steering/recovery effects can be attributed separately under one fixed benchmark contract.

Predeclare repeated runs and fault injections for timeout/provider ambiguity, tool failure, process kill/restart, duplicate wakeup and cancellation; measure recovery success, duplicate effects, cost/latency and accepted quality together.
Define PROMOTE_ASYNC versus KEEP_SYNC_BASELINE from a Pareto/non-inferiority gate rather than pass rate alone, with complete attempt accounting and independent verification.
Revoke the prior READY premise and issue a fresh readiness binding only after this acceptance protocol is stable and compatible with the unified delivery benchmark program.

tasks.title: Define trusted objective supersession and research reset control
expectedOutputs: A typed objective-supersession contract binds exact old/new objective identities, rationale/evidence, target plan and downstream impact.
Trusted CI provides a dedicated supersession publication path while ordinary RESEARCH_SA candidates remain unable to redefine their own objective.
Supersession resets an unfinished target to DRAFT research with stale readiness/worker authority, claim and context removed while retaining historical provenance.
A separate BB-065 migration can use the delivered control to replace the obsolete value-study objective with neutral substrate calibration.

tasks.title: Research feedback lifecycle and cross-episode learning
expectedOutputs: Specify observation/context/finding/impact contracts with exact identity, provenance, uncertainty and missing-context behavior.
Specify application-owned disposition and ACTED/REJECTED/DEFERRED/SUPERSEDED response resolution, recovery and fresh IMPROVED/NO_CHANGE/REGRESSED/UNKNOWN outcomes.
Specify deduplicated cohort-based pattern proposals, counterevidence, systemic mechanism evidence and reinforcement without automatic escalation.
Define additive seams with Observer/Oracle/reconciliation/HOW evolution and neutral benchmark evidence, preserving existing accepted scopes.

Compare reuse and smallest native extension using verified primary evidence; produce exact package/file-level implementation plan, direct dependencies, negative cases and preregistered benchmark/eval protocol for fresh Jev readiness.
